The Womb's reef: today and the reshape (round 2)

Measured with the game's own wave model (no GPU needed), 15 s swell from the south-west, the peel stretch on. Plan views face the beach from the water: the beach is at the top, the left runs to your left. The red circle is the take-off.

What a surfer gets, wave by wave

Today: the first ~120 m peels at a rideable speed but is mostly soft (oval) on bigger days, because big waves trip in deep water well out in front of the take-off; after that the line closes out.

Green: a barrel you can ride, with how long it lasts. Grey: soft, breaks but doesn't barrel. Red: closes out. Amber: the gap where the wave backs off and you can kick out.

From above

Side on: the seabed under each part

Slices along the wave's path, open sea on the left, reef top on the right (viewpoint A). The new reef rises from much deeper water in a short, steep face: that is what makes the wave throw instead of crumble.

Round 2: what changed

The reef's edge is a metre shallower (3.5 m at mid tide, was 4.5), so 6 ft now barrels at mid tide and 4 ft stays soft. The cost: every size moves down one step, so 12 ft now wants high tide (at mid tide its first section closes out). The tide slides the window. The first section barrels at 6–8 ft on low tide, 6–10 ft on mid, 8–12 ft on high. The whole ride (first section, gap, second section) works at 4–6 ft on low, 6–8 ft on mid, 6–12 ft on high; bigger than that, the second section closes out.

The second section stays faster than the first (12–16 m/s against 5–9): turning it further across the swell did not slow it, because it starts as its own small peak and the swell wraps around it. Nothing here is in the game yet.
